g.text: - Read Replicas: Since the system is read-heavy, we use a Leader-Follower

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: DB architecture. All writes (new songs, new users) go to the Leader. All

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: reads (searching, fetching metadata) hit the Follower databases to prevent

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Sharding: As the catalog grows, we partition the database geographically

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: (e.g., US shard, EU shard) or by Artist ID ranges to keep related data

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Cache Management: We place a caching layer (like Redis) in front of the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: database for lightning-fast search and metadata retrieval. We use an LRU

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: (Least Recently Used) eviction policy so when the cache fills up, the oldest,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: least-played data is removed to make room for trending songs.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Global CDNs: We deploy Content Delivery Networks globally (North

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: America, Europe, etc.). Instead of fetching audio from the main S3 bucket

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: every time, users stream it from an edge server physically closest to them,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Chunked & Resumable Uploads: Large audio files are broken into smaller

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: chunks during upload. We use file fingerprinting to track which chunks have

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: successfully uploaded. If the user's internet drops, it acts as a "save

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: point," allowing a multipart upload to resume exactly where it left off

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Processing audio is heavy. We do not want users waiting on a loading

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The Flow: When a raw file lands in S3, it publishes an event. A message

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: broker routes this event to a fleet of backend worker nodes (e.g., utilizing

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: Kafka consumer groups). These workers operate in the background,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: asynchronously transcoding the raw file into adaptive bitrates (64kbps,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - Predictive Buffering (Pre-fetching): The mobile client anticipates the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: user's needs by silently downloading the next few audio chunks (or the next

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: song in a playlist) in the background. If the user drives through a tunnel

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: and loses signal, the song continues playing smoothly from the local buffer.

text.font-family: Lilita One, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 1) Storing 3 PB of data in RAM (like Redis) is financially impossible.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: - The Solution: Instead of calculating cache based on total traffic volume,

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: calculate it based on the hottest catalog items (e.g., caching the top

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: 20% most-played songs results in a highly manageable 60 TB).

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > L1 (Client-Side): Zero-cost local storage directly on user devices

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji
Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > L2 (Edge CDN): The massive 3 PB load is distributed globally using

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: cheap disk storage (SSDs/NVMe). Across 200 global locations, this

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: averages out to just ~15 TB per edge node.

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: > L3 (Internal RAM): Expensive Redis memory is strictly reserved for

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: lightweight, mutable metadata (user profiles, URLs, playlists), keeping the

text.font-family: Excalifont, Xiaolai, sans-serif, Segoe UI Emoji

g.text: RAM footprint to a few hundred gigabytes.
